{{dropinitial|T}}HAT Titus was a Gentil, and not a Iew, and that he was in S. Paules traine, at the lea{{ls}}t the 14 yere after his conuer{{ls}}ion, if not before, we vnder{{ls}}tand by the Epi{{ls}}tle to the Galatians c. 2. And that he continued with him to the very end, appeareth in the {{ls}}econd to Timothee c. 4. Where he maketh mention that he {{ls}}ent him from Rome into Dalmatia, when him{{ls}}elf was {{ls}}hortly after to be put to death.

And therefore although S. Luke neuer name him in the Actes, as neither him{{ls}}elf, yet no doubt he comprehendeth him commonly, when he {{ls}}peaketh thus in the fir{{ls}}t per{{ls}}on plurall: ''Forthwith we {{ls}}ought to goe into Macedonia.
